prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. Describe the spatial understanding this image supports: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). descriptions.rgb: The five frames show a checkout counter directly in front of the camera wearer, with the counter surface and point-of-sale equipment roughly 0.5–1 metre away. In the first three frames, a nearby person or the camera wearer’s own blue-clad torso and bare arm occupies much of the left and centre foreground within arm’s reach, heavily occluding the counter and the space ahead. Across these frames, the viewpoint turns right, shifting the blue-clad body out of the centre and revealing more of the counter, a register or payment terminal, display screens, papers, and shelving behind them. In the fourth and fifth frames, an adult in dark clothing stands behind the counter about 1.5–2 metres in front of the camera wearer, facing generally toward the camera, with the head partly or fully cropped by the upper edge. A white sheet held by that person is within their arm’s reach and about 1–1.5 metres from the camera wearer, while another sheet lies on the counter between them; by the final frame, the person and paper shift slightly left in the image as the camera continues turning right, and a large foreground sign or display remains partly cut off at the right and bottom edges.
